root.name: Grob Opening: Romford Countergambit
root.moves: 1. g4 d5 2. Bg2 Bxg4 3. c4 d4

overview: White plays 1.g4 and Black takes the pawn with ...Bxg4 and then pushes 3...d4 to gain space, answering the long diagonal. Black has an extra pawn and strong centre; White has the bishop pair prospects and queenside play with Qb3 or d3. White's compensation is thin.

white_ideas.idea: Use the long diagonal with Bg2 and Qb3
Attack the d4 pawn with Nf3 and d3
Open lines with b4 or e3

black_ideas.idea: Hold the extra g4 bishop pawn gain and the d4 space

typical_structures.structure: Black d4 pawn space advantage against White fianchetto

character.notes: White gambits a pawn and Black gets a space grab.

gambit.notes: Black can keep the g4 pawn.

structure.notes: Black's d4 pawn restricts White's position; the centre is closed-ish.

approach.notes: The Grob is an anchor for offbeat.

level.notes: Simple ideas but the line is unsound.

character.reason: White has gambited a pawn and play is concrete.

gambit.reason: White offered the g4 pawn and Black has taken it.

soundness.reason: The Grob Gambit is considered unsound.

structure.reason: The centre pawns are not yet fixed.

approach.reason: The Grob is an offbeat anchor.

plans.reason: White hopes for development and the long diagonal.
